title: Sitting Still for Butterflies
description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: sit very quietly near flowers and see if a butterfly comes close.

body.heading: Choose a flower spot
paragraphs: Find a sunny spot near flowers where butterflies like to drink. Sit down on your cushion with your adult and get comfortable.
Butterflies are shy. If you run after them, they fly away. But if you sit as still as a statue, they may forget you are there.

body.heading: Wait and watch
paragraphs: Stay quiet and count slowly in your head. Watch the flowers. A butterfly lands by unrolling a long, curly tongue like a tiny straw to sip the flower's sweet juice.
Look at the colours and patterns on its wings. Are both sides the same? Butterflies often look different with their wings open and closed.

body.heading: Remember the visit
paragraphs: When the butterfly leaves, think about which flower it liked best. Some butterflies visit the same kind of flower again and again.
Back home, draw your butterfly from memory. It does not need to be perfect — it needs to be yours.

takeaway: Butterflies come close to people who sit still and quiet, so patience is the best butterfly tool.
materials: A cushion or mat to sit on
safetyNotes: Never chase or grab butterflies — their wings are easily damaged. Let them come to you, and watch quietly.
screenFreeExtension: Flap a piece of paper gently like a butterfly wing and feel how lightly the air moves.
